metadata.description: Ground truth Clean Architecture compliance annotations for the ERP/CRM dataset

justifications.layer_separation: Modules group related functionality but do not separate domain, application, and infrastructure layers. Models contain both business logic and ORM calls.
justifications.dependency_rule: Domain models import and use the Odoo ORM directly; inner layers know about outer (infrastructure) concerns.
justifications.entity_independence: Model classes inherit from models.Model, making them completely dependent on the Odoo ORM. There is no way to instantiate a domain entity without the framework.
justifications.use_case_layer: Some business operations are placed in service-like methods or wizard classes, but most logic lives in model methods that are also persistence objects.
justifications.testability: Tests require a running Odoo environment and PostgreSQL; unit-testing domain logic in isolation is not possible without significant mocking.
justifications.abstraction_usage: External services (email, payment) are accessed through Odoo abstractions, but core persistence has no interface, preventing swapping the ORM.

evaluations.overall_assessment: Odoo is a highly productive framework-centric ERP, but it makes no attempt to follow Clean Architecture. All layers are collapsed into framework-dependent modules. Suitable as a negative reference example.

justifications.layer_separation: DocType classes serve simultaneously as schema definitions, form renderers, validators, and persistence objects. Layers are fully collapsed.
justifications.dependency_rule: Every document class imports from frappe (the infrastructure framework). Domain logic cannot be used without the full Frappe stack.
justifications.entity_independence: Inheriting from frappe.Document hard-couples every entity to the Frappe ORM, metadata engine, and HTTP layer.
justifications.use_case_layer: Controller functions provide some separation of workflow logic, but they still rely on frappe.db and frappe.get_doc, mixing application and infrastructure concerns.
justifications.testability: Tests must set up a full Frappe site with a MariaDB/PostgreSQL database; domain-level unit testing is impractical.
justifications.abstraction_usage: Frappe provides hooks and override mechanisms but the core domain objects have no interface layer.

evaluations.overall_assessment: ERPNext inherits Frappe's opinionated architecture that prioritises developer productivity over structural separation. It is another strong negative reference example for Clean Architecture.

justifications.layer_separation: Clear server/module/client boundary. Within the server, models and business logic are separated from the RPC protocol, but persistence is still in the model layer.
justifications.dependency_rule: Model classes import from trytond core for ORM functionality; inner layers depend on the framework's ORM layer.
justifications.entity_independence: Models use Tryton descriptors (fields.Char, fields.Many2One) making them dependent on the ORM, but the structure is cleaner than Odoo/ERPNext.
justifications.use_case_layer: Wizards and workflow transitions provide an application-layer abstraction above simple CRUD operations.
justifications.testability: Tests can be run against an in-memory SQLite database; domain logic is more testable than Odoo/ERPNext, though full isolation is not achieved.
justifications.abstraction_usage: The IR layer and module system provide some abstraction, but there are no explicit port/adapter interfaces for external systems.

evaluations.overall_assessment: Tryton shows better modular design and a more structured layering than Odoo or ERPNext. It partially follows Clean Architecture in its server/module separation and wizard-based application layer, but inner domain objects still depend on the ORM.

justifications.layer_separation: Module directories group related files, but each module file mixes database calls, business logic, and sometimes HTML output.
justifications.dependency_rule: SugarBean base class (Active Record) blends persistence and domain logic; all modules depend directly on the database layer.
justifications.entity_independence: All domain objects extend SugarBean which includes direct PDO/SQL access. Entities cannot exist independently of the database.
justifications.use_case_layer: There is no identifiable application service or use case layer; workflow logic is embedded directly in module classes.
justifications.testability: A test framework exists, but most tests require a database connection because domain objects are Active Records.
justifications.abstraction_usage: No interfaces or abstractions for persistence, email, or other external services; everything is hardcoded to concrete implementations.

evaluations.overall_assessment: SuiteCRM represents a classic legacy PHP application with virtually no architectural separation. It is an extreme negative example for Clean Architecture evaluation.

justifications.layer_separation: Distinct Entity, Repository, Service, and Controller namespaces exist and are consistently applied across the codebase.
justifications.dependency_rule: Services depend on Repository interfaces, not on concrete Doctrine classes; controllers depend on services, not on repositories. The inward dependency direction is mostly respected.
justifications.entity_independence: Entity classes hold state and some domain logic, but they still have some awareness of the persistence layer (e.g., attribute handling tied to the ORM).
justifications.use_case_layer: Service classes act as an application layer, encapsulating business workflows and coordinating between entities and repositories.
justifications.testability: DI container and repository interfaces enable mocking; unit tests for services are feasible without a real database.
justifications.abstraction_usage: Repository interfaces abstract the persistence layer; service interfaces allow dependency injection. External integrations use adapter classes.

evaluations.overall_assessment: EspoCRM demonstrates noticeably better architectural discipline than other PHP CRMs in this dataset. Its consistent use of DI, repository patterns, and service layers partially aligns with Clean Architecture, making it a useful intermediate example.

justifications.layer_separation: PHP page scripts mix HTML generation, business logic, SQL queries, and session handling in a single file. No recognisable architectural layers.
justifications.dependency_rule: Dependencies point in all directions; class files include global functions, SQL calls, and HTML output indiscriminately.
justifications.entity_independence: Domain classes (e.g., Societe, Facture) contain raw SQL queries and direct database access, making them completely dependent on infrastructure.
justifications.use_case_layer: No application service or use case layer is present. Actions are implemented as procedural page scripts.
justifications.testability: A PHPUnit test suite exists but coverage is low; testing domain logic requires database connections because of the Active Record pattern.
justifications.abstraction_usage: No interfaces or abstractions for any external dependency. The database handle ($db) is passed directly to every domain class constructor.

evaluations.overall_assessment: Dolibarr is the clearest example of a non-layered, procedural/Active-Record codebase in this dataset. It serves as a strong baseline 'zero Clean Architecture' reference.

justifications.layer_separation: Symfony bundle structure enforces clear separation: Entity, Repository, Provider/Manager (service), Controller, and Form layers are distinct and consistently named.
justifications.dependency_rule: Entities know nothing about Symfony; repositories depend on Doctrine interfaces; services depend on repository interfaces. A few Symfony annotations in entities create minor violations.
justifications.entity_independence: Doctrine entities are plain PHP objects with annotations/attributes. They are not coupled to Symfony directly, though Doctrine mapping metadata is embedded via annotations.
justifications.use_case_layer: Manager and Provider classes serve as an application service layer, but they are not explicitly named 'use cases' and occasionally mix orchestration with infrastructure calls.
justifications.testability: Extensive unit and integration test suites. Services can be tested with mock repositories; Symfony DI container facilitates test environment configuration.
justifications.abstraction_usage: Repository interfaces, event dispatchers, and service contracts (interfaces) are used throughout. Some concrete Symfony dependencies in manager classes reduce the score.

evaluations.overall_assessment: OroCRM is the closest to Clean Architecture among the PHP projects in this dataset. Its Symfony foundation and DDD-influenced bundle design provide strong layering. It is a good positive reference, though it falls short of full Clean Architecture due to framework coupling in some service layers.

justifications.layer_separation: Maven module boundaries enforce strict layer separation. Separate modules exist for domain model, repository interfaces (DAO API), repository implementations, service interfaces (BL), and service implementations.
justifications.dependency_rule: API modules (interfaces only) are compiled against by inner layers; implementation modules depend on the API. The dependency graph is largely acyclic and inward-pointing. Some legacy ADempiere code still violates this.
justifications.entity_independence: Domain value objects (e.g., OrderId, MoneyWithCurrency) are plain Java classes with no framework dependencies. JPA annotations exist in some models but are kept in a separate infrastructure module.
justifications.use_case_layer: Business logic (BL) interfaces and implementations provide a clear use-case / application service layer. Use cases are named with domain intent (e.g., IOrderBL.closeOrder).
justifications.testability: Unit tests cover domain and service logic with JUnit 5 and Mockito, without needing a database. Integration tests are separate. High test coverage in business-critical modules.
justifications.abstraction_usage: All cross-layer communication happens via Java interfaces. Spring DI wires concrete implementations. External systems (e-mail, document storage) accessed through dedicated port interfaces.

evaluations.overall_assessment: metasfresh is the strongest Clean Architecture implementation in this dataset. Its multi-module Maven layout, interface-first design, and use of domain value objects demonstrate deliberate adherence to Clean Architecture and DDD principles. Minor violations exist in older ADempiere-derived code.

justifications.layer_separation: OSGi plugin system enforces a strong module boundary. Within a plugin, Model (PO-based), Process (use case), and UI layers are conventionally separated.
justifications.dependency_rule: OSGi service interfaces allow inward dependencies between plugins, but generated model classes (MOrder, MInvoice) extend PO which is tied directly to the database layer.
justifications.entity_independence: All business model classes extend the PO (Persistent Object) base class, binding every entity to the database access logic. No pure domain entities exist.
justifications.use_case_layer: Process classes provide a recognisable application service / use case layer, called explicitly and separate from model classes.
justifications.testability: The Active-Record PO pattern makes domain unit testing difficult. Integration tests run against a live database. Some process classes can be tested in isolation with mocking.
justifications.abstraction_usage: OSGi services and interface-based plugin communication provide good abstraction at the module level, partially compensating for the lack of abstraction within modules.

evaluations.overall_assessment: iDempiere achieves good separation at the plugin boundary level through OSGi, but falls short internally because the Active Record base class (PO) couples every domain model to the database. A partial Clean Architecture example with strong module isolation.

justifications.layer_separation: Module directories separate modules from each other, but within a module the CRMEntity subclass handles persistence, business logic, and often view rendering together.
justifications.dependency_rule: CRMEntity base class accesses the database directly; all module classes depend on it. No inversion of this dependency exists.
justifications.entity_independence: Every domain class extends CRMEntity which contains PDO database calls. Entities cannot be instantiated without a live database connection.
justifications.use_case_layer: Handler classes add some event-based workflow logic, providing a rudimentary separation for certain operations, but most business logic remains in CRMEntity subclasses.
justifications.testability: A PHPUnit test suite exists but coverage is minimal; domain testing without a database is effectively impossible.
justifications.abstraction_usage: The Vtlib library provides some utility abstractions, and the handler system adds a degree of indirection, but no formal port/adapter interfaces exist.

evaluations.overall_assessment: Vtiger CRM inherits SugarCRM's legacy Active Record architecture and adds only superficial architectural improvements. It is another strong negative example, slightly better than SuiteCRM due to the handler system.
